title: Put a silicone swimming cap onto a headform
instruction: Stretch the swimming cap over the headform. Cover the crown, leave the face clear, and release it without tearing the cap.
setup: A rigid adult headform, 190 × 160 × 240 mm, fixed to a 140 × 130 mm base. A separate silicone cap has a 150 × 140 mm opening, 90 mm dome, 0.8 mm wall and 3 mm rolled rim. Both hands start holding its front and back rim 55 mm above the crown and 120 mm toward the robot from the head; actual contact is checked before the trial. Both grippers have 40 × 24 × 3 mm silicone-faced extensions; the arms stand on 100 mm risers. The nose faces the left arm. Restore the photographed layout; README gives coordinates.
scoring: 1.0 if the intact cap covers the crown, its rim surrounds the head below the crown and above the eyes, and it stays fitted for three seconds after release. The crown gap must be at most 2 cm; the rim must stay within the 5.5 cm below to 7.5 cm above head-centre band, with the front edge at least 3 cm above head centre. 0.5 for the surrounding rim and clear face without the crown/release condition; 0.25 for the crown within 2.5 cm and face clear. Otherwise 0. A torn cap scores 0. Use the video and a ruler.
fidelity: The cap is an elastic shell with self-contact and a rolled rim. A pinch uses a native constraint only when the rim is between closing finger faces; it releases on opening and breaks at 40 N or 0.08 Nm. Material response is approximate and the head is rigid. The robot must stretch, place and release the cap; no fitted shape is prescribed. The finite grip connects to the native gripper and transmits reaction loads.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: Fitting a swimming cap requires stretching a thin elastic object around a curved surface while keeping the face clear.
